dataset: physical setting: network design, drainage basins, geological succession

network_design.state_extent: N lat 11d31' - 18d45', E long 74d12' - 78d40'; 31 districts, 233 taluks
network_design.depth_semantics: dug wells tap phreatic aquifer mostly <=20 m; piezometers 20-100 m tap phreatic + deeper aquifers; levels may differ at same place
network_design.analysis_scope: phreatic-aquifer wells only; piezometer levels excluded from water-level/fluctuation maps
network_design.schedule: Jan + Nov: 1st-10th; May + Aug: 20th-31st; quality samples once yearly in May; monthly monitoring at select Bengaluru Metropolitan wells
network_design.district_analysis_note: 27 districts analysed: Bangalore Rural+Ramnagara, Kolar+Chikballapura, Bellary+Vijayanagara, Gulbarga+Yadgir merged in GEMS/WIMS software
network_design.purpose: 4 seasonal snapshots; annual fluctuation vs same month prior year; decadal fluctuation vs same-month decadal mean

units: coastal plain: 300 km Karwar-Mangalore, <=40 km wide, 0-200 m amsl, west-flowing rivers
Malnad: steep ranges/valleys east of coast, 50-100 km wide, 200 m to 1872 m (Kudremukh); Cauvery, Tungabhadra originate here
southern/eastern plateau: rolling topography with sporadic hills, 600-1000 m amsl
physiography.climate: coastal/hilly per-humid to sub-humid; plains sub-humid to semi-arid; east-of-ghats rain shadow, drought prone
physiography.seasons: dry Jan-Feb; pre-monsoon Mar-May (squally, hail); SW monsoon Jun-Sep (bulk of rain, sets in first week June); post/NE monsoon Oct-Dec (depressions/cyclones)

tributaries.Krishna: Bhima, Malaprabha, Ghataprabha, Tungabhadra, Upper Krishna, Vedavathi
tributaries.Cauvery: Arkavathi, Hemavathi, Kabini, Shimsha, Suvarnavathi, Upper Cauvery (Arkavathi/Shimsha/Pennar/Ponnaiyar rise near Nandi hills/Bengaluru)

drainage.district_lists_note: machine-text district lists truncate mid-list; kept verbatim with truncation flag; Plate-II map is visual-lane OCR

succession_young_to_old: Tertiary-Mesozoic: Deccan Trap basalt (hard massive & vesicular)
Bhima Series (Lower Palaeozoic-upper Precambrian): quartzite, sandstone, limestone, shale, conglomerate
Kaladgi Series (Upper Precambrian): quartzite, sandstone, limestone, shale, conglomerate
Dharwar system volcanics + schists (Lower Precambrian): greenstone, metasediments
Archaean Peninsular Gneissic Complex: gneiss, granite, charnockite, khondalite
key_points: majority of state: Peninsular gneiss, granite, Dharwarian schists (Archaean); basalts (Deccan Traps) in north; Bhima/Kaladgi sedimentaries small northern area; alluvium narrow coastal + stream belts
majority of monitoring stations sit in granitic-gneissic terrain

crystalline/consolidated rocks lack primary porosity (except vesicular basalt zones); groundwater held in secondary porosity: weathering, fracturing, jointing; solution cavities in limestone form good aquifers
